A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same F-CLIPScore study despite retitling and reformatting. All seven pages of v2 and eleven pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original OHD-Caps evaluations, LLaVA data-filtering experiments evaluated on POPE, embedding analyses and appendix robustness experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds OHD-Caps comparisons with additional methods and encoder configurations in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The sentence-and-noun averaging metric in Equation 1, augmented training loss in Equation 2 with alpha 0.3, and data-filtering procedure are retained. Evaluating additional encoders does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the COCO, Flickr30k and NoCaps subsets of OHD-Caps, LLaVA pretraining data, POPE evaluation and Wikipedia-derived nouns for perturbations. The added experiments expand model configurations within existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 5 adds CECLIP and NegCLIP as evaluated OHD-Caps comparators. The original comparisons involving CLIPScore, OHD-loss training and alternative data-filtering methods remain.

E3.justification: Tables 5–6 introduce evaluations using CLIP-B/32, CLIP ViT-H, SigLip ViT-L and EVA-CLIP ViT-L alongside the retained CLIP-L setting. Existing accuracy metrics, filtering rates and stated training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds a targeted test of whether gains persist across encoder architectures and sizes. The embedding analysis and Tables 3–4 perturbation and word-type ablations are retained. Relabeling noun injection as replacement does not establish a new perturbation experiment: v2 already mentioned replacement, and its rates and results are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averaging over ten runs with different seeds, and Table 3 retains means and standard deviations over five seeds. Tables 5–6 add point estimates without introducing a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 substantially broaden the reported evidence to trained alternatives and multiple backbones. Table 5 reports F-CLIPScore with CLIP-B/32 at 56.0/53.2/43.0 versus NegCLIP at 52.8/40.8/23.4 across the three subsets. Existing Tables 1–4 retain their values apart from equivalent rounding. Section 5.1 corrects the gap to OHD-trained CLIP from 21.8–38.6 to 17.6–37.4 percentage points and correctly assigns the 0.1-point training gain to NoCaps rather than Flickr30k.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and losses in Equations 1–2 are unchanged, with no added assumptions, proofs or derivations. The new cited statement about linear parser runtime supplies explanation rather than a new theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The title and abstract soften the assertion that encoder capacity is already adequate to the claim that it is not necessarily a major limiting factor. The proposed metric, data-curation contribution and headline 39.6-point OHD-Caps and 4.9-point POPE gains remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 changes the interpretation from a possible vision-representation shift alongside improved text discrimination to more pronounced text-representation changes and relatively minor vision changes. The limitations concerning untested SFT and multilingual generalization are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4 replaces the parser-time description of less than one second per sentence with an average of 170 ms and adds parallelization and complexity information. These refine documentation of the existing parser; training hyperparameters, hardware, training times and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting CECLIP, NegCLIP, SigLip, EVA-CLIP and parser complexity. Section 2 also changes its characterization of the vision-encoder explanation attributed to Liu et al. from the root cause to one of the causes, while retaining the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: The title and author block change, and grammar, cross-references and several explanatory passages are refined. The main section sequence and most of the narrative are retained; the licenses section loses its Appendix B designation.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two columns to one, with different typography and substantially resized or relocated displays. Figure 2 changes from vertically stacked to horizontally arranged panels, and Tables 5–6 are added. Table 3 relabels injection rates as replacement rates, and Table 2 clarifies the pre-SFT evaluation stage.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons and encoder evaluations strengthen validation of the existing metric. Correcting the Section 5.1 discrepancies, documenting parser runtime more precisely and moderating the abstract improve accuracy and clarity. These are bounded gains to the same core study. Figure 2's more crowded legend is a small presentation drawback that does not outweigh the stronger evidence and reporting corrections.
